talkwheel.jaymoskingdoms.jaymoskingdoms_: I have seen the far side of the night. I would speak of the old blood.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.refuse.0: You have had your bottle. The moon must turn before I open my hand again.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.refuse.1: Not yet. What I give is not given twice in a season.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.refuse.2: Patience. You have taken from me lately; come when the dark has changed.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.poor.0: Sixty in silver. I do not give such things for less.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.poor.1: Your purse is light, friend. So is my offer.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.poor.2: Come back with silver. Sixty pieces, no fewer.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.deal.0: Take it, and keep it corked. Drink it when the sky is black and the moon is not there. Do not say I gave it.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.deal.1: A fair price. Wait for the moon that has no light, and drink it then. You will not wake the same.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.old_blood.deal.2: It is done. Under a dark moon it is a door; any other night it is only a bottle.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.gossip.old_blood.0: My gran said the old ones keep a little blood in bottles, for those who choose to follow them.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.gossip.old_blood.1: They say there is a night when the moon shows no face, and what is done in that dark is not undone.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.gossip.old_blood.2: A traveller once swore a man drank something red under a black sky, and was a stranger by the next dusk.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.gossip.old_blood.3: Some are bitten, and some are not bitten at all. Some go to the dark on their own feet.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.gossip.old_blood.4: Ask the old man in the crypt, they say. If he thinks you have seen enough, he may open his hand.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.gossip.old_blood.5: Never drink what an Elder pours when the moon is lit. It is only wine then. Or so I was told.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.gossip.old_blood_hun: We found a bottle once, on one we had beaten down. Dark as wine. We broke it. Do not drink what an Elder gives.
A beaten Elder leaves blood in glass. Never let it near a mouth, least of all on a moonless night.
The worst of them are the ones who turned willingly, in the dark of the moon. No bite, no fear, no cure.
If you see a bottle of that red, smash it. If you see someone holding one under a black moon, run.
speech.jaymoskingdoms.lair_hunt.seen.0: The crypt is near. Stakes ready, torches high.
speech.jaymoskingdoms.lair_hunt.seen.1: It sleeps by day. We take it by day. No bottles, no bargains, only the stake.
speech.jaymoskingdoms.lair_hunt.seen.2: Find the coffin. Whatever sleeps in it does not wake before dusk.
speech.jaymoskingdoms.lair_hunt.tore.2: It will not rest here again.
gui.jaymoskingdoms.story.hint.270: A coffin shut by day lets you sleep until dusk. When every player is sleeping or resting, the sun skips to the evening. A stake driven into a sleeper still kills.
gui.jaymoskingdoms.story.hint.271: A tailor sews a deep-hooded cloak. With the hood up, noon only stings you, and folk see a hooded stranger instead of your pale face. Holy dread still finds you.
gui.jaymoskingdoms.story.hint.272: When the moon is new, the night belongs to them: the Elder hunts twice as often, bleeders come down from the sky, the fever climbs faster, and leaps and claws hit harder.
gui.jaymoskingdoms.story.hint.273: When a realm grows sure of a vampire, guards with torches and stakes, and a priest, come looking for the crypt by day. You can hear them in your heartbeat. A coffin and a shrine can be picked up and moved.
gui.jaymoskingdoms.story.hint.274: Some say the Elder will part with his own blood in a bottle, if you have seen enough of the other side, and that a moon with no light is the night to drink it.
